blocks.content: The Supreme Court is the guarantor of the Fundamental Rights of the citizens and the guardian of the Constitution.

rows: Enforcement of Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights
Applicable throughout the entire territory of India
Limited to the state or specific territorial jurisdiction of the High Court
Guaranteed Fundamental Right; Supreme Court cannot refuse to exercise jurisdiction
Discretionary power; High Court may refuse to exercise writ jurisdiction

items: Original jurisdiction under Article 131 does NOT extend to pre-Constitution treaties, agreements, or covenants.
Advisory opinion given by the Supreme Court under Article 143 is purely advisory and NOT binding on the President.
Special Leave Petition (Article 136) is a discretionary power that applies to any court or tribunal in India, EXCEPT military tribunals.
While Article 32 writ jurisdiction is restricted only to Fundamental Rights, High Courts under Article 226 can issue writs for ordinary legal rights as well.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Original jurisdiction under Article 131 exclusively covers federal disputes between the Union and States or between States.
The Supreme Court is the defender and guarantor of Fundamental Rights through its original writ jurisdiction under Article 32.
Appellate jurisdiction encompasses Constitutional (Article 132), Civil (Article 133), Criminal (Article 134) matters, and discretionary Special Leave Petitions (Article 136).
Under Article 143, the President can seek the non-binding advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or public importance.
As a Court of Record (Article 129), its judgments hold perpetual evidentiary value and it possesses the power to punish for contempt of court.
